short: the scheduler's edge around the pure core
is: What stands between the pure scheduling core (domain/schedule) and the world: the ports read into each ticket's facts, the phase run folders, the tick's phase steps over the core's placement, the trace of every tick, and the scheduler that stays up (`zaf spawn --watch`).
conventions: The core decides and this module reads and writes: where a ticket sits always comes from domain::schedule::place
record.rs is the one reader and writer of a phase run folder under .zaf/phases/
State labels are output only, set from each ticket's place and never read back as state
Every module has its tests in <module>/tests.rs

fs.name: ask.rs
fs.role: tick step 5: every question the scheduler raises (getting nowhere, a failed wait with no on-fail, an overdue check wait, a dead dependency, a cycle, an unchallenged epic), each ending with a marker read back from the board so no cause has two open questions; raised under spawn.lock once the open questions are read again under it

fs.name: binary.rs
fs.role: the running image's identity against the start path, settled over two looks, `--version` with a deadline, exec with the same arguments

fs.name: gather.rs
fs.role: open tickets with a phase list into TicketFacts and what the tick reads beside them (priority label, ready_since), adjacent model actions folded, an unreadable ticket named and skipped; gather_one for `zaf spawn phase`, gather_for for the dry run, status and the hub

fs.name: labels.rs
fs.role: tick step 2's label sync: question, blocked and stale-to-ready set from the place, never over a claim or done, written only when it differs; a failed write is named and the rest goes on

fs.name: lock.rs
fs.role: `.zaf/scheduler.lock` held with flock for life, its one line naming the holder; running() for readers, which never lock

fs.name: record.rs
fs.role: the run folder: task, action, head, size, instance, pid or the inline mark of the tick that runs it, output, questions, head-end, exit last

fs.name: request.rs
fs.role: `.zaf/tick.request`: ask() appends a line only while a scheduler runs; Requests reads each complete line once on a size-and-mtime mark and empties the file past 16 KiB

fs.name: scheduler.rs
fs.role: the loop, pure behind a Host: one tick at a time for who asked, the timer, restart only between ticks with no request waiting, stop on a signal; Memory keeps the placement as a cache

fs.name: shadow.rs
fs.role: the dry run's `placement` as JSON, a lane ticket with its weight; decides nothing

fs.name: tick.rs
fs.role: may_start, the one gate the tick and `zaf spawn phase` both pass; the held lines; tick steps 3 to 6 over the lane, slots from the live model runs; the placement handed back for the scheduler's cache

fs.name: tick/
fs.role: support.rs (the steps' test helpers) and tests.rs

fs.name: ticks.rs
fs.role: `.zaf/ticks.jsonl` under `.zaf/ticks.lock`: append, cut, read, the last tick's time from the file's end

fs.name: trace.rs
fs.role: the tick's trace line, pure: short places, the moves against the last line, the count line with the open epics' done tasks, the 14-day cut

fs.name: trace/
fs.role: listing.rs (what `zaf spawn trace` prints) and tests

notes: The process that hosts the loop (the lock, signals, the exec of a new binary) is cli/scheduler.rs; the hub runs the same loop through app/spawn/watch.rs
The rulings behind it are in zaf/memory/decisions/scheduler-rulings.md (R5 labels as output, R24 the trace)
ask/, binary/, gather/, labels/, lock/, record/, request/, scheduler/, shadow/ and ticks/ hold only tests.rs
